question: What is the waiting period for maternity expenses under the Oriental Happy Family Floater Policy?
ground_truth: Maternity expenses are covered only after the policy has been continuously in force for 24 months (under the Diamond Plan).

question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases under the Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani policy?
ground_truth: Pre-existing diseases are covered after a waiting period of 48 months (4 years) of continuous coverage from the policy's inception date, provided they were declared at the time of application and accepted by the insurer.

question: Are robotic surgeries covered as a modern treatment method under the Navi Health Super Top Up policy?
ground_truth: Yes, robotic surgeries are listed among the covered Modern Treatment Methods, along with stereotactic radiosurgery, bronchial thermoplasty, and stem cell therapy, wherever medically indicated.

question: Is AYUSH treatment (Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) covered under Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani?
ground_truth: Yes, inpatient care treatment under AYUSH systems of medicine is covered up to the sum insured limit specified in the policy schedule, at any AYUSH hospital.

question: Is cosmetic surgery covered under the New India Top-Up Mediclaim Policy?
ground_truth: No, change of life or cosmetic/aesthetic treatment of any description is excluded, along with plastic surgery not necessitated by an accident or illness.

question: Are hazardous or adventure sports injuries covered under the Star Health Senior Citizens Red Carpet policy?
ground_truth: No, expenses for treatment necessitated by participation as a professional in hazardous or adventure sports -- such as para-jumping, rock climbing, mountaineering, or scuba diving -- are excluded under Code Excl 09.

question: What is the room rent sub-limit under the Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani policy?
ground_truth: Room rent, boarding, and nursing expenses are limited to 2% of the sum insured, subject to a maximum of Rs 5,000 per day; ICU/ICCU charges are limited to 5% of the sum insured, subject to a maximum of Rs 10,000 per day.

question: What is the cataract treatment sub-limit under the Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani policy?
ground_truth: Cataract treatment is subject to a sub-limit of 25% of the sum insured or Rs 40,000 per eye per policy year, whichever is lower.

question: How does the pre-existing disease waiting period compare between Star Health's Arogya Sanjeevani policy and its Senior Citizens Red Carpet policy?
ground_truth: Arogya Sanjeevani has a longer pre-existing disease waiting period of 48 months, while the Senior Citizens Red Carpet policy's waiting period is shorter, at 12 months.

question: How does the Daily Hospital Cash Allowance differ across the Silver, Gold, and Diamond plans of the Oriental Happy Family Floater Policy?
ground_truth: Daily Hospital Cash Allowance is not available under the Silver plan. Under Gold, it is 0.1% of sum insured (Rs 600-1,000/day); under Diamond, it is 0.1% of sum insured (Rs 1,200-2,000/day); both are capped at 10 days per illness and an overall 1.5% of sum insured.
